history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration include environmental considerations in core category strategies to mitigate environmental risks.
history.administration_response: Relevant United Nations Secretariat solicitations refer to the Way Forward: Environment Strategy for Peace Operations 2023–2030, which outlines performance indicators and requirements in areas such as renewable energy, freshwater use, greenhouse gas emissions, wastewater treatment and solid waste management. The current approach reflects a measured effort to align procurement practices with the Sustainable Development Goals, balancing environmental priorities with the need to maintain competition and inclusivity. The Administration provided a statement of requirements for modular ablution structures that refers to the Environmental Strategy for peace operations and field-based political missions.
history.board_assessment: Notwithstanding the example provided, the Board sees no measurable progress regarding the implementation of the recommendation, which therefore remains under implementation.

history.recommendation_text: In paragraph 451 of its report, the Board recommended that the Administration include environmental considerations in core category strategies to mitigate environmental risks.
history.reference_raw: Recommendations contained in the report of the Board of Auditors for the 12 -month period ended 30 June 2024 (A/79/5 (Vol. II)
history.sg_progress: Please refer to number 64 of annex II to the Board’s report A/80/5 (Vol. II) for the Administration’s comments. The Administration has taken significant steps to mainstream environmental considerations into core categories with a view to maximizing impact, and achievements such as the turnkey renewable energy contract demonstrate steps forward. However, the liquidity situation and the evolving peacekeeping landscape, through upcoming mission closures, startup activities for Haiti, contingency plans and the UN80 Initiative, have led to the reprioritization of resources to focus on critical operational support. Over the coming months, the Office of Supply Chain Management will aim to incorporate environmental considerations into its core categories to the extent practical and commensurate with the requirements of its client entities.
